newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 8.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Regulations compelling local authorities to submit quarterly reports on their financial status to the provincial affairs and constitutional development ministry is expected to be promulgated next week.

- Concern was growing that the private sector was losing confidence in government's low-cost housing programme, industry sources said. Developers and banks faced costly bureaucratic delays and a lack of capacity at provincial government level.

- Iscor Ltd is considering mothballing its Pretoria steel mill, endangering 1,400 jobs, as the plant has failed to climb out of the red despite bids to cut costs and change to stainless steel production.

- Weapons manufacturer Denel was in preliminary talks with at least three Mediterranean and Persian Gulf states on the possible sale of the Rooivalk combat helicopter, acting MD Seshi Chonco said on Monday.

- Magistrate's court officials fought on Monday to protect former Zimbabwean president Canaan Banana, 62, from publicity when he appeared for indictment before the High Court on 11 allegations of homosexual offences including the rape of a State House aide.
BUSINESS REPORT

- East Rand Proprietary Mines Ltd, which forms part of the Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd mining house, is to close its subsidiary, Benoni Gold Mining Co Ltd, because of low grades and the falling bullion price, company executives said on Monday.

- The JSE's all gold index on Monday slumped 5,06 percent or 48,2 points to 903,9 points, a fresh four-and-a-half year low. The index was dragged won by bullion, which lost 6,45 dollars to 318 dollars after dipping 8,10 dollars on Friday.

- Gold continued its downhill slide on global markets on Monday, bouncing down nearly seven dollars to 318 dollars an ounce at the afternoon fix in London from Friday's 324,45 dollars. It fell even further, to 313,60 in late London trade.

- Negotiations to resolve a strike by about 4,500 workers in the sugar industry collapsed in panic on Monday as union and employer representatives dissolved the talks when they received word that as many as 400 striking workers were preparing to storm the meeting, negotiators said.

- The Competition Board has launched an investigation to determine whether South African Breweries Ltd has a monopoly in the alcoholic beverage industry and whether any agreements it has in the industry constitute a restrictive practice.

- Teljoy the television, information technology and telecommunications group, sold its 10 percent stake in Teljoy Cellular to Vodacom for 20.1 million rand in the first half of the past financial year and bought it back after the year-end for 23.2 million rand, its latest annual report said.

- Bridgestone Corp, the Japan-based tyre multinational, faces its first significant labour dispute in South Africa just months after it bought Fedstone from Murray & Roberts for 290 million rand and announced a further investment of 220 million rand earlier this year.
SAKE BEELD
- The sharp drop in gold price on Monday from previous days continues and dealers expect a further drop to 300 dollars.
THE STAR
- People's justice in the form of people's courts and mob killings of suspects is taking hold in Gauteng as crime-scarred commuities reject disintegrating policing and justice systems.
- Around 40,000 fans snapped up the much sought after tickets on the opening day of bookings for Irish bank U2's tour, on Monday.

- Gauteng provincial legislature member, Oupa Monareng of the African National Congress, said on Monday he had survived two attempts to kill him in Soweto at the weekend and that he had waited for more than an hour for an ambulance to take him to the Baragwanath Hospital.
- Scientists on Monday said the area around the Mars Pathfinder site was hit by devastating floods billions of year ago.
- Gold continued its plunge on Monday, hitting a 12-year low.
